touches.text: The launcher walks the words. `cairn cairn foo bar` (the long form) means "tell the cairn device to run foo with argument bar". At each level: is the next word a machine here? Step into it and take the next word. Is it a script in this level's bin/? Run it, pass back the result, done. Neither? It is a bus verb: send it to this level over the bus. So `cairn foo bar baz`: foo is a device; it has a machine bar; bar's bin/ has baz, so baz runs. No bar machine? bar goes to foo over the bus. Each check is one directory lookup, so it is fast. WHY scripts first: scripts are the simple path; the bus is the route to what a device answers itself.

Any device or machine may have a bin/ beside its code. That folder IS its list of shortcuts: add a file to add one, delete it to remove one. A shortcut is a script that calls the long form (eg `cairn superclaude` -> `cairn cc superclaude`; `cairn show temp` -> `cairn recovery show temp`), which also saves the walk from searching farther, or does work itself (eg install). Shortcuts live beside what they serve (RULE 1). `cairn foo` whose first word is not a device means `cairn cairn foo`: top-level shortcuts are the cairn device's bin/.
A new shortcut needs no watch. Most instance bins are links to their class bin, so the shortcut is reachable the moment its file lands; the build's proof is the whole guarantee.

Scripts are Python wherever possible, run by Cairn's own interpreter, so one file works on every platform. Platform-specific ones match their platform: executable or .sh on Linux; .bat, .cmd or .ps1 on Windows.

Commit: the proofs of the component the ticket changed, since RULE 1 bounds a change to its component. Passing them puts the component in service, yellow: proven where it changed, not yet measured against what depends on it. In service needs only the best we can do now: 80% trust.

Owns the Claude Code hooks: mail check, the turn-shape and ask scans, the gates on record writes and deletes. Anything that adapts CC specifically to Cairn goes in the CC device, and every one of CC's scripts lives here.

RULE 1, ENCAPSULATION: every component talks to every other only through that component's public interface: a device's is the bus plus any client tool it publishes; a machine's or tool's is what its entry declares. Nothing outside a device reaches into its code, skills included. A ticket builds inside its own component, and its proofs measure only that component. WHY: it limits a change to the component that made it.
Physics: the encapsulation_holds sieve in build_inspector, a device-path check. Code in device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo except a tool foo publishes. Inside one device nothing is checked.

Declaring a new instance rotates, explicitly or implicitly: --new rotates explicitly, no flag rotates implicitly, --name overrides both. -amm Reading (superclaude is the rescue service's launcher, cairn/devices/cc/superclaude; none of these needs a folder prepared by hand): - `cairn superclaude --new` always rotates explicitly to the next undeclared n (cc_1 when cc_0 is declared, cc_2 when cc_1 is, and so on), then declares, wires and launches it. - `cairn superclaude` with no flag rotates implicitly: it starts cc_0 when cc_0 is free, and when cc_0 is taken (running) it rotates as --new does. - `cairn superclaude --name <x>` uses exactly x and overrides all of that: it declares x if absent, then launches it. - The declared folder commits through the door in the same act, so the house tree is not left dirty and crossings are not refused. - The one CC inference here: "implicitly" is read as taken (running) cc_0 means rotate, while a declared-but-stopped cc_0 is simply started. Tickets: aa05710a5124 reshapes to this; d13859e2ae46 is the implicit rotation; 0f7a8cada1ca names the next undeclared n. - akiendelllinux_orchestrator

Each stage moves from the model to deterministic code once a proof a hollow build could not pass can hold it; hypothesize stays with the model longest. Validate sends a local miss back to hypothesize and a structural one back to design. A build that finds new work spawns children that enter at decompose.

A rule not yet enforced is made into a ticket now, never left floating as prose. So ticket f5dbfddea8c6 makes the rewrites it proposed at the remaining sites (the press office, PROOF.md). Where a site names a rule whose physics is not built, it names that rule's real ticket id, cast now if none exists; the word "ticket" with no id behind it does not count. - CC
Owns the CC launcher (superclaude): starts Claude Code with Cairn's session contract, in its own memory-capped cgroup. WHY: Claude can OOM the box.
A rule CLAUDE.md names that is still prose is a bug with a ticket. WHY: unenforced rules used to pile up, so a law now forbids them; any that stands is a bug. -amm
